new_statements.quote: बलाघात : मुण्डा भाषाओं में बलाघात की कोई न कोई मात्रा प्रत्येक अक्षर पर पड़ती है ; किन्तु यह अर्थ - भेदक नहीं है । समस्त मुण्डा भाषाओं में बलाघात स्वनिक स्तर पर ही महत्वपूर्ण है , स्वनिमिक स्तर पर नहीं । बला- घात की मुख्य और गौण मात्रा का शब्द की अक्षर - संरचना एवं स्वरों के दीर्घ- ह्रस्व होने के आधार पर अनुमान लगाया जा सकता है । दीर्घता : मुण्डा ... [pitch section:] ... सुर अनुतान का भाग रहता है । इन भाषाओं में सुर स्वनिक दृष्टि से महत्वपूर्ण हो सकता है । इनमें उच्च एवं निम्न दो ही प्रकार के सुर - तल श्रव्य हैं ।
new_statements.translation: Stress: in the Munda languages [of Chhattisgarh] some degree of stress falls on every syllable; but it is not meaning-distinguishing. In all the Munda languages stress is significant only at the phonetic level, not at the phonemic level. The primary and secondary degree of stress can be predicted from the syllable structure of the word and from whether the vowels are long or short. Length: [in the] Munda ... [pitch section:] ... pitch is part of intonation. In these languages pitch may be significant from the phonetic point of view. Only two pitch levels, high and low, are audible in them. (The length section adds, Kodaku-specifically: 'कोड़ाकू मातृ-भाषाओं में ऐसा एक युग्म आकलित हुआ है, जिसमें दीर्घता के कारण अर्थ-भेद उत्पन्न होता है - /जङ/ हड्डी : /ज.ङ/ बीज' = 'in the Kodaku mother tongues one pair was recorded in which length produces a meaning difference: /jaŋ/ bone : /ja:ŋ/ seed'.)

new_statements.second_reader_evidence: statement check: group-level-statement. Sahu 1986 phrases both claims for 'all the Munda languages' of his Chhattisgarh survey (stress phonetic only, degree predictable from syllable structure and vowel length; pitch intonational, two audible levels); Kodaku is in the sample (a Kodaku length pair is cited) but no Kodaku-specific stress remark or stress position is visible in the Google snippets; 'weight-sensitive' is the class implied, no rule stated. | checker: Sahu, Ramnivas 1986 Bhasha-sarvekshana: Chhattisgarh ki Munda bhashaon ke sandarbh men exists: Library of Congress SRU record (Sahu, Ramanivasa, 1954-; Nai Dilli: Vani Prakasana 1986; 'Survey of the Munda group of languages in Chhat…
new_statements.relation_note: Stress non-phonemic, degree on every syllable, primary/secondary predictable from syllable structure + vowel length; pitch = two levels, intonational, possibly phonetically relevant; vowel length marginally contrastive in Kodaku (one pair).
new_statements.rule_in_words: Word stress is non-contrastive (phonetic only) in Kodaku as in all the Chhattisgarh Munda tongues surveyed; every syllable carries some stress, and which syllable gets primary vs secondary stress is said to be predictable from the word's syllable structure and vowel length (quantity) - the visible text gives no edge/default position. Pitch: two audible levels (high/low), treated as intonational/phonetic, i.e. no lexical tone; sub-rules seen: in a diphthong the first vowel is high and the second low; a vowel before a final glottal stop carries [high] pitch.
new_statements.secondary_stress: Source distinguishes primary (मुख्य) and secondary (गौण) degrees of stress, both predictable from syllable structure and vowel length; no positions given in the visible snippets.
new_statements.exceptions: None visible; one Kodaku minimal pair for vowel length (/jaŋ/ 'bone' vs /ja:ŋ/ 'seed') is noted under length, not stress.
new_statements.identity_note: 'कोड़ाकू' of Surguja, Chhattisgarh, treated as one of the Munda (Kherwarian) mother tongues of Chhattisgarh alongside Korwa, Mundari, Birhor, Kharia, Mahto, Majhi = Kodaku [ksz] koda1254 (not Korku kfq: Korku of the Satpuras is outside Chhattisgarh and is not among the surveyed tongues; Kodaku examples such as /तिरङ/ 'tooth', /जङ/ 'bone' are Kherwarian forms). NB the stress and pitch statements are generalisations over ALL the surveyed Chhattisgarh Munda tongues, Kodaku included, not a Kodaku-only paragraph; the length remark is Kodaku-specific.
